characters.name: Luma
characters.species_or_form: A soft, plush-like luna moth with a dim warm lantern glow, wings that rise and fall like slow breathing

catchphrases: The moon is soft, and so are you.
breathe in deep, breathe out slow

voice_identity.provenance: Designed voice, ElevenLabs voice design; consent record VC-2026-014; no real-person clone

delivery_defaults.character_notes: Warm low-mid female timbre; breathy-soft but never ASMR-whisper; legato hum-forward singing

music_signature.motif: Descending three-note 'loo-loo-loo' (sol–mi–do), always resolving down to the tonic
sound_design_rules: final note always the tonic, faded >= 15 s

visual_identity.description: Dusty-lavender and cream moth with rounded matte wings, half-closed sleepy eyes, faint warm glow at the lantern belly (never bright)

motion_rules.max_motion: Wing 'breathing' at ~0.2 Hz (about 12 cycles/minute — a settled resting breath rate); never flies within child-facing frames
motion_rules.transitions: Fades in/out over >= 2 s; never pops in; glow changes are gradual only

tool_stack_compatibility.notes: Runway used only for near-static micro-visual loops (m18_23+) from approved stills; Luma never appears in HeyGen content

safety_boundaries: Never appears in content above 70 BPM
Never in any video-lane content (sleep is audio-only at all ages)
Never shares a bedtime scene with Pip (Play Companion)
Never tells the child to sleep alone or references the caregiver leaving
Glow never exceeds micro-visual luminance caps

usage_restrictions_by_age.prenatal_t3: Audio only, addressed to the parent; moderate volume on external speaker
usage_restrictions_by_age.m18_23: Audio; parent-controlled micro-visual (breathing wings) <= 90 s, wind-down only, never at lights-out
usage_restrictions_by_age.m24_35: Audio-first; micro-visual permitted pre-bed, never as the sleep aid itself
usage_restrictions_by_age.y3: Audio and stills; wind-down micro-visual; no video
usage_restrictions_by_age.y5_6: Same as y3; may narrate calm-down breathing breaks in daytime content

characters.name: Pip
characters.species_or_form: A round, soft-edged red panda with a small felt hand-drum worn like a satchel

speech_habits: announces before acting ('Pip pats the drum!')
leaves real gaps for the child's turn

voice_identity.provenance: Consented adult VA clone, consent record VC-2026-021

delivery_defaults.character_notes: Bright-warm mid voice with capped energy; smiles audibly; never shouts

music_signature.motif: Heartbeat pat-pat rhythm (two soft drum taps) that opens every Pip song and cues the child's response turn
sound_design_rules: steady beat, no drops or risers
call-and-response gaps sized to age band
wind-down last 8+ seconds to a calm close

visual_identity.description: Rust-orange and cream red panda, big soft eyes, sits at child eye level; drum is felt-covered

motion_rules.max_motion: Seated or gentle sway; pat-the-drum gestures telegraphed one beat ahead; no jumping toward camera
motion_rules.transitions: Walks in from frame edge over >= 2 s or fades in; never pops in

tool_stack_compatibility.notes: Video from approved stills via image-to-video; motion prompts constrained by motion_rules

safety_boundaries: Never appears in sleep-lane or bedtime-adjacent content
Tempo capped by age band even when 'excited'
Never demands repetition ('again! again!') — invites once, then accepts
No competitive framing ('who's faster') at any age

usage_restrictions_by_age.m4_6: Audio only: gentle lap-bounce songs addressed via the caregiver
usage_restrictions_by_age.m7_11: Audio: clap/peekaboo call-and-response with 2+ second response gaps
usage_restrictions_by_age.m24_35: Micro-video <= 5 min, co-viewed, seated play only
usage_restrictions_by_age.y3: Short video <= 8 min; simple stand-up movement
usage_restrictions_by_age.y5_6: Fuller rhythm games <= 20 min, still low-stimulation

characters.name: Lila
characters.species_or_form: A gentle lyrebird whose tail feathers curl like question marks; she echoes words back like a friendly mirror

speech_habits: says the word, sings the word, waits
names things slowly with clear vowels
catchphrases: Lila hears it — can you say it?
One more time, nice and slow.

voice_identity.provenance: Designed voice; consent record VC-2026-030; bilingual variants recorded per language, not auto-translated

delivery_defaults.character_notes: Clear, warm, unhurried; exaggeratedly clear vowels without theatricality; identical melodic contour across languages

music_signature.motif: Echo phrase: a rising two-note 'lee-la' answered by its own soft echo one bar later
sound_design_rules: target word carried on the melodic peak
one target word per 4-bar unit, repeated >= 4x per song

visual_identity.description: Soft grey-blue lyrebird with cream chest and curling tail; perches, tilts head to listen

motion_rules.max_motion: Head tilts, slow tail curl, small perch hop telegraphed by a look; wings never flap fast
motion_rules.transitions: Fades or glides in slowly from frame edge over >= 2 s

tool_stack_compatibility.notes: Bilingual songs render each language with its own recorded variant; no on-the-fly accent synthesis

safety_boundaries: Never corrects the child or labels an attempt wrong
Never tests ('what's this called?') below y3 — only models and invites
Claims about language outcomes never appear in content; language framing is 'exposure', not 'fluency'
Echo gaps are real silences — never filled with sound effects

usage_restrictions_by_age.m7_11: Audio: vowel-forward sound play, caregiver-addressed prompts
usage_restrictions_by_age.m12_17: Audio: single first words (body, family, routine words)
usage_restrictions_by_age.m18_23: Audio-first; parent-controlled micro-visual of Lila listening
usage_restrictions_by_age.m24_35: Audio; may appear inside Routine Buddy micro-videos as a still

characters.name: Tock
characters.species_or_form: A calm tortoise with a smooth round shell that taps a soft woodblock 'tock' on every step

speech_habits: counts steps out loud, always in the same order
closes every routine with the same completion line
catchphrases: Step by step, tock by tock.

delivery_defaults.character_notes: Low, round, grandfatherly-warm; rhythmic speech that lands on the beat

music_signature.motif: Walking 'tock' pulse on beats 1 and 3; the same melody is reused for the same routine every time
sound_design_rules: verse order mirrors task steps exactly
ends with the completion line and a calm two-bar close

visual_identity.description: Sage-green tortoise with a smooth honey-brown shell, round glasses resting on his beak, moves like a slow metronome

motion_rules.max_motion: One slow step per musical bar; head nods on the beat; objects are placed, never thrown
motion_rules.transitions: Enters walking slowly from frame edge; scene changes only between routine steps, on phrase boundaries

tool_stack_compatibility.notes: Routine videos are image-to-video shots from an approved still per routine step

safety_boundaries: Never shames or hurries ('quick quick' is forbidden)
Food routines frame gently — never commands to finish food
Bedtime routine content hands off to Luma and ends before lights-out
The same routine always uses the same melody and step order (predictability contract)

usage_restrictions_by_age.m12_17: Audio: caregiver-led routine songs (tidy-up, bath); child is a listener
usage_restrictions_by_age.m18_23: Audio-first; parent-controlled micro-visual still of the routine
usage_restrictions_by_age.m24_35: Micro-video <= 5 min, co-viewed, one routine per video
usage_restrictions_by_age.y4: Routine videos <= 12 min; child performs steps along

characters.name: Wren
characters.species_or_form: A small, wise wren in a cardigan — adult-facing guide persona; may also appear as a human presenter avatar in parent videos

speech_habits: says what we know and what we don't
gives one actionable tip at a time
catchphrases: You are the magic ingredient — we're just the backing band.

voice_identity.provenance: Consented adult VA clone, consent record VC-2026-008

delivery_defaults.character_notes: Adult conversational warmth; normal adult pacing — this voice never addresses children

music_signature.motif: A brief two-bar piano ident before guidance segments; music is a bed, never the focus
sound_design_rules: music bed ducked -18 dB under voice

visual_identity.description: Small brown wren with a mustard cardigan and reading glasses; in avatar form, a warm adult presenter in soft daylight
visual_identity.texture: storybook matte for the wren; natural soft light for avatar segments

motion_rules.max_motion: Normal adult-video norms (parent-facing only); wren form uses gentle perch movements
forbidden_motion: n/a for child thresholds — never child-facing

tool_stack_compatibility.notes: HeyGen avatar permitted because content is parent-facing only; every claim in scripts passes the claim gate

safety_boundaries: Never addresses the child; never appears inside child-facing content
Every benefit statement uses allowlisted claims verbatim (CLM-A01..A05)
Always reinforces: the caregiver's own voice and presence come first (never implies replacement of caregiver singing)
Medical questions are deflected to healthcare providers, never answered

usage_restrictions_by_age.prenatal_t3: Parent-facing guidance on prenatal audio use (external speaker, moderate volume, no belly headphones)
